findings.evidence: Line 167: `SectionChartData.chartProduct_apply (C₃ := ...) ... (b := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (F₁ →L[ℝ] F₂)) ...` must match a goal whose RHS has no `id` applied, under the comment '`ContinuousLinearMap.id` applies as the identity.'
findings.fix: Prove it by `rw [SectionChartData.chartProduct_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply]` (or `simp [SectionChartData.chartProduct_apply]`) and drop the named-argument restatement.
findings.issue: `chartProduct_hom` is closed by the term `SectionChartData.chartProduct_apply` with every argument named. It only type-checks because `ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ _ f` reduces to `f` by definition through the coercion; the comment notes this, but the proof never states it.

findings.evidence: Lines 168–200: four `fun … ↦ by simpa using mulAux_eq_smul_add_smul hb … fun i ↦ by filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset (h₁ i | h₂ i) (Lp.coeFn_add … | Lp.coeFn_smul …)] … simp only [chartProduct_apply, …]` blocks.
findings.fix: Factor out lemmas such as `chartProduct_add_left_ae`/`chartProduct_smul_left_ae`/`chartProduct_add_right_ae`/`chartProduct_smul_right_ae` (a.e. on `C₃.image i`, using `h₁`/`h₂`) and build `mulₗ` from them with one-line `simpa`s.
findings.issue: The four linearity laws of `mulₗ` are four near-copies of the same `simpa using mulAux_eq_smul_add_smul … filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset … (Lp.coeFn_add/coeFn_smul …)] … simp only [...]` block. Each re-proves a.e. linearity of `chartProduct` in one variable without exposing it as a lemma, and the four simp chains break together on any rename.

summary: `chartProduct_hom` relies on the definitional unfolding of `ContinuousLinearMap.id` instead of an explicit lemma, and `mulₗ` repeats the same a.e.-linearity argument four times instead of factoring it out.
